```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(plotly)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE)

data("ny_noaa", package = "p8105.datasets")

weather_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2010-01-01"), date <= as.Date("2010-12-31")) |>
  transmute(
    id,
    date,
    month = as.integer(format(date, "%m")),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    invalid_pair = !is.na(tmin) & !is.na(tmax) & tmin > tmax,
    season = factor(
      case_when(
        month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
        month %in% 3:5 ~ "Spring",
        month %in% 6:8 ~ "Summer",
        TRUE ~ "Fall"),
      levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall"))) |>
  mutate(
    tmax = if_else(invalid_pair, NA_real_, tmax),
    tmin = if_else(invalid_pair, NA_real_, tmin))

monthly_df =
  weather_df |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarize(
    n_tmax = sum(!is.na(tmax)),
    n_tmin = sum(!is.na(tmin)),
    n_prcp = sum(!is.na(prcp)),
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_tmin = mean(tmin, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_prcp = mean(prcp, na.rm = TRUE),
    wet_percent = 100 * mean(prcp > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")

set.seed(6961)
scatter_df =
  weather_df |>
  filter(!is.na(tmin), !is.na(tmax)) |>
  slice_sample(n = 4000)

coverage_df =
  weather_df |>
  summarize(
    `Maximum temperature` = sum(!is.na(tmax)),
    `Minimum temperature` = sum(!is.na(tmin)),
    Precipitation = sum(!is.na(prcp)))

# Shared styling keeps axes and hover text legible in each panel.
plot_font = list(family = "Trebuchet MS, sans-serif", size = 14, color = "#17324d")
```

Weather
=======================================================================

Row {data-height=110}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### A year of station observations

Explore **`r format(nrow(weather_df), big.mark = ",")` station-day records** from
**`r n_distinct(weather_df$id)` New York stations**. Monthly summaries use all
available measurements; the scatterplot uses a reproducible sample of 4,000
complete temperature pairs. **Hover** for details, **click a legend** to hide a
series, or **drag** to zoom. Double-click a plot to reset. Read **Data & methods**
for coverage and interpretation.

Row {data-height=350}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Monthly mean daily temperatures

```{r temperature-line}
plot_ly(monthly_df, x = ~month) |>
  add_trace(
    y = ~mean_tmax, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
    name = "Daily maximum", line = list(color = "#225c94", width = 3),
    marker = list(color = "#225c94", size = 7),
    text = ~paste0(month.name[month], "<br>Observed station-days: ",
      format(n_tmax, big.mark = ",")),
    hovertemplate = "%{text}<br>Mean maximum: %{y:.1f} °C<extra></extra>") |>
  add_trace(
    y = ~mean_tmin, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
    name = "Daily minimum", line = list(color = "#086d75", width = 3, dash = "dash"),
    marker = list(color = "#086d75", size = 7, symbol = "diamond"),
    text = ~paste0(month.name[month], "<br>Observed station-days: ",
      format(n_tmin, big.mark = ",")),
    hovertemplate = "%{text}<br>Mean minimum: %{y:.1f} °C<extra></extra>") |>
  layout(
    font = plot_font,
    margin = list(l = 65, r = 25, b = 75, t = 15),
    xaxis = list(title = "Month (2010)", tickvals = 1:12, ticktext = month.abb,
      showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE),
    yaxis = list(title = "Temperature (°C)", gridcolor = "#e3ebf2"),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.16)) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```

### Mean daily precipitation by month

```{r precipitation-bars}
plot_ly(
  monthly_df, x = ~month, y = ~mean_prcp, type = "bar", textposition = "none",
  marker = list(color = "#225c94"),
  text = ~paste0(month.name[month], "<br>Observed station-days: ",
    format(n_prcp, big.mark = ","), "<br>Wet days (>0 mm): ",
    round(wet_percent, 1), "%"),
  hovertemplate = "%{text}<br>Mean precipitation: %{y:.2f} mm/day<extra></extra>") |>
  layout(
    font = plot_font,
    margin = list(l = 70, r = 20, b = 75, t = 20),
    xaxis = list(title = "Month (2010)", tickvals = 1:12, ticktext = month.abb,
      showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE),
    yaxis = list(title = "Precipitation (mm/day)", rangemode = "tozero",
      gridcolor = "#e3ebf2"),
    showlegend = FALSE) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```

### Daily minimum and maximum temperatures

```{r temperature-scatter}
plot_ly(
  scatter_df, x = ~tmin, y = ~tmax, color = ~season,
  colors = c("#225c94", "#086d75", "#a15316", "#76519a"),
  type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
  marker = list(size = 5, opacity = 0.45),
  text = ~paste0("Station: ", id, "<br>Date: ", date, "<br>Season: ", season),
  hovertemplate = paste0("%{text}<br>Minimum: %{x:.1f} °C",
    "<br>Maximum: %{y:.1f} °C<extra></extra>")) |>
  layout(
    font = plot_font,
    margin = list(l = 65, r = 15, b = 75, t = 30),
    xaxis = list(title = "Daily minimum (°C)", gridcolor = "#e3ebf2"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Daily maximum (°C)", gridcolor = "#e3ebf2"),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.15, font = list(size = 12))) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```

Data & methods
=======================================================================

Column
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data source and preparation

The dataset is `ny_noaa` from the **p8105.datasets** package, originally drawn
from NOAA's Global Historical Climatology Network Daily data. The complete
course dataset covers 1981–2010. This dashboard filters it to **January 1–December
31, 2010** before summarizing or sampling. Each row represents one station on
one date.

Temperatures are stored as character values in tenths of a degree Celsius; I
convert them to numeric values and divide by 10. Precipitation is in tenths of a
millimeter and is also divided by 10. The resulting units are **°C** and **mm**.

In `r sum(weather_df$invalid_pair)` records, the reported minimum exceeds the
maximum. I set both temperatures in those records to missing while retaining
their precipitation values. Missing measurements are excluded separately for
each variable; they are never replaced by zero.

#### Coverage after cleaning

```{r coverage-table}
data.frame(
  Measurement = names(coverage_df),
  `Observed station-days` = format(as.integer(coverage_df[1, ]), big.mark = ","),
  `Missing (%)` = round(100 * (1 - as.numeric(coverage_df[1, ]) / nrow(weather_df)), 1),
  check.names = FALSE) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE)
```

These counts use the **`r format(nrow(weather_df), big.mark = ",")` records in
2010** as their denominator. Some stations measure precipitation but do not
measure temperature, so coverage differs substantially across variables.

#### How to read the charts

**Line chart.** Each point is a monthly mean of all nonmissing station-day
measurements for that variable. Maximum and minimum temperatures can have
different denominators. Hover text gives the number of contributing records.

**Bar chart.** Each bar is mean precipitation per observed station-day in a month,
including observed zeros. This is not a monthly rainfall total. Hover text also
shows the proportion of observed days with precipitation greater than zero.

**Scatterplot.** Each point is one of 4,000 randomly selected station-days with
both temperatures observed and minimum no greater than maximum. Sampling is
without replacement, using `set.seed(6961)`. Seasons are winter (December–February),
spring (March–May), summer (June–August), and fall (September–November).

#### Interpretation and limitations

The monthly temperature lines show a strong seasonal pattern, while the sampled
temperature pairs show warmer minima and maxima during summer. The highest
mean daily precipitation in this dataset occurs in
**`r month.name[monthly_df$month[which.max(monthly_df$mean_prcp)]]`**.

These are descriptive summaries of available station records. Stations with more
observed days receive more weight; the set of reporting stations can change by
month and variable. The charts are not area-weighted estimates for New York
State, and one year cannot establish a long-term climate trend. Differences
between months may reflect both weather and reporting coverage.

#### Reproducibility and references

The dashboard loads the package dataset directly. No downloads or package
installations occur during knitting, and all charts run in the browser without a
Shiny server. **Source Code** in the navigation contains the dashboard's R Markdown
source. This dashboard is the separate solution to Homework 4, Problem 2.
To rebuild both homework components, open the R Project and run
`source("build.R")` from the project root.
